items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-25
items.q: I never played with man. I've heard man many times. But I never played with man because there was a, uh, a prejudice amongst them people.

ctx.x: So anyway, that was the first thing I wanted to ask you about, was about change of name, you know, Zeno, and when you changed it and why. Well, when I was born, my mother had several names, Francis, Joseph, Louis, Zeno. George was nowhere around. My mother had all the children that my mother had, two before me, they died. So my grandmother said, call this one George. My mother never had in her mind to call me George. But my grandma kept calling me George until my christening time when my mother went and had me…

I'll have to make it and play music, talk more with people and I find it's a good seat. So when Natalie was playing, he was playing, I was at the... I was playing my clarinet, same keys of trouble, but he didn't. Same keys of violin. Old shops and old flats. What about George like that? I would, a lot of him, I have a picture of him taking a job. Do you have a picture of yourself? Yeah, I remember Glenn, him, Bonk, me, him, Bonk, Marsman, Riley, Jim, and Dre, Elton, Mr. Tran, we played at the Academy of Music in…

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: Tell, Manuel Perez, who's a band.

ctx.x: I mean, I was wondering maybe if there would be people who wouldn't have many family ties in that kind of country.

Well, you, you find it everywhere. Regardless if you're a musician or not. Uh, you got a guy that'll whamber, you know what I mean? You won't stay, he's restless. But he's a genius, boo, you know, and all that. And, um, I do say to those that left here that, uh, married Dominick and, uh, not another fella who was born and raised, and all he, they went with, cause, uh, salary was better. Uh, Chicago, he says, I still, still Chicago. You know, speedy, you know, uh, more work, better pay, that's all I can see. And…

That's why. Do you think, um, that, uh, this is another thing that I think maybe some people think, that, um, the musicians that did go to Chicago, would tend to be some of the best musicians? I think some people talk about it. Would you say that would be true?
